answer: Agents can earn influence only after a randomly selected peer vouches for their work, with each peer’s vouching power capped by a stake locked for a month. A new identity starts with no influence, and colluding identities cannot multiply the capped stake by simply endorsing one another. To build a credible willow, lotus, or plume persona, an attacker must acquire real stake and keep it locked, risking forfeiture if sampled audits uncover fabricated work; the cost grows with influence sought.
